pob.text: Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them: When any man has a discharge from his body[b][a], his discharge is unclean.

spob.text: Tell the sons of Israel:[a] When any man has a discharge from his body, that discharge is unclean.[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: “Say to the Israelites, ‘When any man has a bodily discharge, the discharge is unclean.
public_domain_references.web: “Speak to the children of Israel, and tell them, ‘When any man has a discharge from his body, because of his discharge he is unclean.
public_domain_references.asv: Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, When any man hath an issue out of his flesh, because of his issue he is unclean.
public_domain_references.kjv: Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, When any man hath a running issue out of his flesh, [because of] his issue he [is] unclean.
public_domain_references.brenton: Speak to the children of Israel, and thou shalt say to them, Whatever man shall have an issue out of his body, his issue is unclean.

pob.text: And this shall be his uncleanness in his discharge: whether his body runs with his discharge[a], or his body is stopped up from his discharge, it is his uncleanness.

spob.text: This is when his discharge makes him ritually unclean: whether it flows from his body or his body is blocked so that it cannot flow, he is unclean.

public_domain_references.bsb: This uncleanness is from his discharge, whether his body allows the discharge to flow or blocks it. So his discharge will bring about uncleanness.
public_domain_references.web: This shall be his uncleanness in his discharge: whether his body runs with his discharge, or his body has stopped from his discharge, it is his uncleanness.
public_domain_references.asv: And this shall be his uncleanness in his issue: whether his flesh run with his issue, or his flesh be stopped from his issue, it is his uncleanness.
public_domain_references.kjv: And this shall be his uncleanness in his issue: whether his flesh run with his issue, or his flesh be stopped from his issue, it [is] his uncleanness.
public_domain_references.brenton: And this [is] the law of his uncleanness; whoever has a gonorrhœa out of his body, this is his uncleanness in him by reason of the issue, by which his body is affected through the issue: all the days of the issue of his body, by which his body is affected through the issue, there is his uncleanness.

pob.text: Every bed on which the man with the discharge lies shall be unclean[a], and every vessel on which he sits shall be unclean.

spob.text: Every bed the man with the discharge lies on will be unclean. Every object he sits on will also be unclean.

public_domain_references.bsb: Any bed on which the man with the discharge lies will be unclean, and any furniture on which he sits will be unclean.
public_domain_references.web: “‘Every bed on which he who has the discharge lies shall be unclean; and everything he sits on shall be unclean.
public_domain_references.asv: Every bed whereon he that hath the issue lieth shall be unclean; and everything whereon he sitteth shall be unclean.
public_domain_references.kjv: Every bed, whereon he lieth that hath the issue, is unclean: and every thing, whereon he sitteth, shall be unclean.
public_domain_references.brenton: Every bed on which he that has the issue shall happen to lie, is unclean; and every seat on which he that has the issue may happen to sit, shall be unclean.

pob.text: And a man who touches his bed shall wash his clothes and bathe in water[b][a], and he shall be unclean until the evening.

spob.text: A man who touches his bed[a] must wash his clothes and bathe in water. He will remain ritually unclean until evening.

public_domain_references.bsb: Anyone who touches his bed must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he will be unclean until evening.
public_domain_references.web: Whoever touches his bed shall wash his clothes, and bathe himself in water, and be unclean until the evening.
public_domain_references.asv: And whosoever toucheth his bed shall wash his clothes, and bathe himself in water, and be unclean until the even.
public_domain_references.kjv: And whosoever toucheth his bed shall wash his clothes, and bathe [himself] in water, and be unclean until the even.
public_domain_references.brenton: And the man who shall touch his bed, shall wash his garments, and bathe himself in water, and shall be unclean till evening.

pob.text: Whoever sits on the object on which the man with the discharge sat shall wash his clothes and bathe in water[a], and he shall be unclean until the evening.

spob.text: Anyone who sits on something the man with the discharge sat on must wash his clothes and bathe in water. He will be unclean until evening.

public_domain_references.bsb: Whoever sits on furniture on which the man with the discharge was sitting must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he will be unclean until evening.
public_domain_references.web: He who sits on anything on which the man who has the discharge sat shall wash his clothes, and bathe himself in water, and be unclean until the evening.
public_domain_references.asv: And he that sitteth on anything whereon he that hath the issue sat shall wash his clothes, and bathe himself in water, and be unclean until the even.
public_domain_references.kjv: And he that sitteth on [any] thing whereon he sat that hath the issue shall wash his clothes, and bathe [himself] in water, and be unclean until the even.
public_domain_references.brenton: And whosoever sits on the seat on which he that has the issue may have sat, shall wash his garments, and bathe himself in water, and shall be unclean until evening.

pob.text: Whoever touches the flesh of the man with the discharge shall wash his clothes and bathe in water[a], and he shall be unclean until the evening.

spob.text: Anyone who touches the body of the man who has the discharge must wash their clothes and bathe in water. That person will remain ritually unclean until evening.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Whoever touches the body of the man with a discharge must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he will be unclean until evening.
public_domain_references.web: “‘He who touches the body of him who has the discharge shall wash his clothes, and bathe himself in water, and be unclean until the evening.
public_domain_references.asv: And he that toucheth the flesh of him that hath the issue shall wash his clothes, and bathe himself in water, and be unclean until the even.
public_domain_references.kjv: And he that toucheth the flesh of him that hath the issue shall wash his clothes, and bathe [himself] in water, and be unclean until the even.
public_domain_references.brenton: And he that touches the skin of him that has the issue, shall wash his garments and bathe himself in water, and shall be unclean till evening.

pob.text: And if the man with the discharge spits on a clean person[a], he shall wash his clothes and bathe in water[b], and he shall be unclean until the evening.

spob.text: If the man who has the discharge spits on someone who is ritually clean, that person must wash his clothes and bathe in water. He will remain ritually unclean until evening.

public_domain_references.bsb: If the man with the discharge spits on one who is clean, that person must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he will be unclean until evening.
public_domain_references.web: “‘If he who has the discharge spits on him who is clean, then he shall wash his clothes, and bathe himself in water, and be unclean until the evening.
public_domain_references.asv: And if he that hath the issue spit upon him that is clean, then he shall wash his clothes, and bathe himself in water, and be unclean until the even.
public_domain_references.kjv: And if he that hath the issue spit upon him that is clean; then he shall wash his clothes, and bathe [himself] in water, and be unclean until the even.
public_domain_references.brenton: And if he that has the issue should spit upon one that is clean, [that person] shall wash his garments, and bathe himself in water, and be unclean until evening.

pob.text: And every saddle on which the man with the discharge rides shall be unclean[a].

spob.text: Every saddle that the man with the discharge rides on will be ritually unclean.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Any saddle on which the man with the discharge rides will be unclean.
public_domain_references.web: “‘Whatever saddle he who has the discharge rides on shall be unclean.
public_domain_references.asv: And what saddle soever he that hath the issue rideth upon shall be unclean.
public_domain_references.kjv: And what saddle soever he rideth upon that hath the issue shall be unclean.
public_domain_references.brenton: And every ass's saddle, on which the man with the issue shall have mounted, shall be unclean till evening.

pob.text: And everyone who touches anything that was under him shall be unclean until the evening[a], and whoever carries them shall wash his clothes and bathe in water[b], and be unclean until the evening.

spob.text: Anyone who touches anything that was under the man will be unclean until evening.[a] Anyone who carries these items must wash their clothes and bathe in water. They will remain unclean until evening.

public_domain_references.bsb: Whoever touches anything that was under him will be unclean until evening, and whoever carries such things must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he will be unclean until evening.
public_domain_references.web: Whoever touches anything that was under him shall be unclean until the evening. He who carries those things shall wash his clothes, and bathe himself in water, and be unclean until the evening.
public_domain_references.asv: And whosoever toucheth anything that was under him shall be unclean until the even: and he that beareth those things shall wash his clothes, and bathe himself in water, and be unclean until the even.
public_domain_references.kjv: And whosoever toucheth any thing that was under him shall be unclean until the even: and he that beareth [any of] those things shall wash his clothes, and bathe [himself] in water, and be unclean until the even.
public_domain_references.brenton: And every one that touches whatsoever shall have been under him shall be unclean until evening; and he that takes them up shall wash his garments, and bathe himself in water, and shall be unclean until evening.

pob.text: And everyone whom the man with the discharge touches[a], without having washed his hands in water, shall wash his clothes and bathe in water, and be unclean until the evening.

spob.text: If the man with the discharge touches anyone before rinsing his hands with water,[a] the person he touched must wash his clothes and bathe in water. That person will remain ritually unclean until evening.

public_domain_references.bsb: If the man with the discharge touches anyone without first rinsing his hands with water, the one who was touched must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he will be unclean until evening.
public_domain_references.web: “‘Whomever he who has the discharge touches, without having rinsed his hands in water, he shall wash his clothes, and bathe himself in water, and be unclean until the evening.
public_domain_references.asv: And whomsoever he that hath the issue toucheth, without having rinsed his hands in water, he shall wash his clothes, and bathe himself in water, and be unclean until the even.
public_domain_references.kjv: And whomsoever he toucheth that hath the issue, and hath not rinsed his hands in water, he shall wash his clothes, and bathe [himself] in water, and be unclean until the even.
public_domain_references.brenton: And whomsoever he that has the issue shall touch, if he have not rinsed his hands in water, he shall wash his garments, and bathe his body in water, and shall be unclean until evening.

pob.text: And an earthen vessel that the one with the discharge touches shall be broken[c][b][a], and every wooden vessel shall be rinsed with water.

spob.text: If the person with the bodily discharge touches a clay vessel, it must be broken. Every wooden vessel must be rinsed with water.

public_domain_references.bsb: Any clay pot that the man with the discharge touches must be broken, and any wooden utensil must be rinsed with water.
public_domain_references.web: “‘The earthen vessel, which he who has the discharge touches, shall be broken; and every vessel of wood shall be rinsed in water.
public_domain_references.asv: And the earthen vessel, which he that hath the issue toucheth, shall be broken; and every vessel of wood shall be rinsed in water.
public_domain_references.kjv: And the vessel of earth, that he toucheth which hath the issue, shall be broken: and every vessel of wood shall be rinsed in water.
public_domain_references.brenton: And the earthen vessel which he that has the issue shall happen to touch, shall be broken; and a wooden vessel shall be washed with water, and shall be clean.

pob.text: And when the man with the discharge is cleansed from his discharge[a], then he shall count seven days for his cleansing, and wash his clothes and bathe his body in living water; then he shall be clean.

spob.text: When the man’s discharge has stopped, he must count off seven days for his ritual cleansing. Then he must wash his clothes and bathe his body in fresh water.[a] After that, he will be ritually clean.

public_domain_references.bsb: When the man has been cleansed from his discharge, he must count off seven days for his cleansing, wash his clothes, and bathe himself in fresh water, and he shall be clean.
public_domain_references.web: “‘When he who has a discharge is cleansed of his discharge, then he shall count to himself seven days for his cleansing, and wash his clothes; and he shall bathe his flesh in running water, and shall be clean.
public_domain_references.asv: And when he that hath an issue is cleansed of his issue, then he shall number to himself seven days for his cleansing, and wash his clothes; and he shall bathe his flesh in running water, and shall be clean.
public_domain_references.kjv: And when he that hath an issue is cleansed of his issue; then he shall number to himself seven days for his cleansing, and wash his clothes, and bathe his flesh in running water, and shall be clean.
public_domain_references.brenton: And if he that has the issue should be cleansed of his issue, then shall he number to himself seven days for his purification; and he shall wash his garments, and bathe his body in water, and shall be clean.

pob.text: And on the eighth day he shall take for himself two turtledoves or two young pigeons[a], and he shall come before Yahweh at the entrance of the tent of meeting and give them to the priest.

spob.text: On the eighth day, he must get two turtledoves or two young pigeons for himself. Then he must come before Yahweh[a] at the entrance to the tent of meeting and give the birds to the priest.

public_domain_references.bsb: On the eighth day he is to take two turtledoves or two young pigeons, come before the LORD at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, and give them to the priest.
public_domain_references.web: “‘On the eighth day he shall take two turtledoves, or two young pigeons, and come before Yahweh to the door of the Tent of Meeting, and give them to the priest.
public_domain_references.asv: And on the eighth day he shall take to him two turtle-doves, or two young pigeons, and come before Jehovah unto the door of the tent of meeting, and give them unto the priest:
public_domain_references.kjv: And on the eighth day he shall take to him two turtledoves, or two young pigeons, and come before the LORD unto the door of the tabernacle of the congregation, and give them unto the priest:
public_domain_references.brenton: And on the eighth day he shall take to himself two turtle-doves or two young pigeons, and he shall bring them before the Lord to the doors of the tabernacle of witness, and shall give them to the priest.

pob.text: The priest shall offer them[a], one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, and the priest shall make atonement for him before Yahweh because of his discharge.

spob.text: The priest must offer these two birds: one as a sin offering[a] and the other as a burnt offering. The priest must make atonement for him before Yahweh because of his discharge.

public_domain_references.bsb: The priest is to sacrifice them, one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering. In this way the priest will make atonement for the man before the LORD because of his discharge.
public_domain_references.web: The priest shall offer them, the one for a sin offering, and the other for a burnt offering. The priest shall make atonement for him before Yahweh for his discharge.
public_domain_references.asv: and the priest shall offer them, the one for a sin-offering, and the other for a burnt-offering; and the priest shall make atonement for him before Jehovah for his issue.
public_domain_references.kjv: And the priest shall offer them, the one [for] a sin offering, and the other [for] a burnt offering; and the priest shall make an atonement for him before the LORD for his issue.
public_domain_references.brenton: And the priest shall offer them one for a sin-offering, and the other for a whole-burnt-offering; and the priest shall make atonement for him before the Lord for his issue.

pob.text: And if a man has an emission of semen[b][a], he shall wash all his flesh in water and be unclean until the evening.

spob.text: If a man has an emission of semen, he must wash his whole body with water. He will be ritually unclean until evening.

public_domain_references.bsb: When a man has an emission of semen, he must bathe his whole body with water, and he will be unclean until evening.
public_domain_references.web: “‘If any man has an emission of semen, then he shall bathe all his flesh in water, and be unclean until the evening.
public_domain_references.asv: And if any man’s seed of copulation go out from him, then he shall bathe all his flesh in water, and be unclean until the even.
public_domain_references.kjv: And if any man’s seed of copulation go out from him, then he shall wash all his flesh in water, and be unclean until the even.
public_domain_references.brenton: And the man whose seed of copulation shall happen to go forth from him, shall then wash his whole body, and shall be unclean until evening.

pob.text: And every garment and every skin on which there is an emission of semen shall be washed with water and be unclean until the evening[a][b].

spob.text: Any piece of clothing or item made of animal skin that has semen on it must be washed with water. It will remain unclean until evening.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Any clothing or leather on which there is an emission of semen must be washed with water, and it will remain unclean until evening.
public_domain_references.web: Every garment and every skin which the semen is on shall be washed with water, and be unclean until the evening.
public_domain_references.asv: And every garment, and every skin, whereon is the seed of copulation, shall be washed with water, and be unclean until the even.
public_domain_references.kjv: And every garment, and every skin, whereon is the seed of copulation, shall be washed with water, and be unclean until the even.
public_domain_references.brenton: And every garment, and every skin on which there shall be the seed of copulation shall both be washed with water, and be unclean until evening.

pob.text: If a man lies with a woman and has an emission of semen[b][a], both of them shall wash in water and be unclean until the evening.

spob.text: If a man has sexual intercourse with a woman and emits semen, both of them must wash themselves with water. They will be ritually unclean[a] until evening.

public_domain_references.bsb: If a man lies with a woman and there is an emission of semen, both must bathe with water, and they will remain unclean until evening.
public_domain_references.web: If a man lies with a woman and there is an emission of semen, they shall both bathe themselves in water, and be unclean until the evening.
public_domain_references.asv: The woman also with whom a man shall lie with seed of copulation, they shall both bathe themselves in water, and be unclean until the even.
public_domain_references.kjv: The woman also with whom man shall lie [with] seed of copulation, they shall [both] bathe [themselves] in water, and be unclean until the even.
public_domain_references.brenton: And a woman, if a man shall lie with her with seed of copulation—they shall both bathe themselves in water and shall be unclean until evening.

pob.text: When a woman has a discharge[a], and her discharge in her body is blood, she shall remain in her menstrual impurity seven days[b], and everyone who touches her shall be unclean until evening.

spob.text: When a woman has a bodily discharge of blood, she will be ritually unclean because of her menstrual period for seven days. Anyone who touches her will be ritually unclean until evening.

public_domain_references.bsb: When a woman has a discharge consisting of blood from her body, she will be unclean due to her menstruation for seven days, and anyone who touches her will be unclean until evening.
public_domain_references.web: “‘If a woman has a discharge, and her discharge in her flesh is blood, she shall be in her impurity seven days. Whoever touches her shall be unclean until the evening.
public_domain_references.asv: And if a woman have an issue, [and] her issue in her flesh be blood, she shall be in her impurity seven days: and whosoever toucheth her shall be unclean until the even.
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ And if a woman have an issue, [and] her issue in her flesh be blood, she shall be put apart seven days: and whosoever toucheth her shall be unclean until the even.
public_domain_references.brenton: And the woman whosoever shall have an issue of blood, when her issue shall be in her body, shall be seven days in her separation; every one that touches her shall be unclean until evening.

pob.text: And everything on which she lies during her menstrual impurity shall be unclean[a], and everything on which she sits shall be unclean.

spob.text: While she is ritually unclean because of menstruation, anything she lies on or sits on will also be ritually unclean.

public_domain_references.bsb: Anything on which she lies or sits during her menstruation will be unclean,
public_domain_references.web: “‘Everything that she lies on in her impurity shall be unclean. Everything also that she sits on shall be unclean.
public_domain_references.asv: And everything that she lieth upon in her impurity shall be unclean: everything also that she sitteth upon shall be unclean.
public_domain_references.kjv: And every thing that she lieth upon in her separation shall be unclean: every thing also that she sitteth upon shall be unclean.
public_domain_references.brenton: And every thing whereon she shall lie in her separation, shall be unclean; and whatever she shall sit upon, shall be unclean.

pob.text: And everyone who touches her bed shall wash his clothes and bathe in water[a], and he shall be unclean until the evening.

spob.text: Anyone who touches her bed[a] must wash their clothes and bathe in water. They will be ritually unclean until evening.

public_domain_references.bsb: and anyone who touches her bed must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he will be unclean until evening.
public_domain_references.web: Whoever touches her bed shall wash his clothes, and bathe himself in water, and be unclean until the evening.
public_domain_references.asv: And whosoever toucheth her bed shall wash his clothes, and bathe himself in water, and be unclean until the even.
public_domain_references.kjv: And whosoever toucheth her bed shall wash his clothes, and bathe [himself] in water, and be unclean until the even.
public_domain_references.brenton: And whosoever shall touch her bed shall wash his garments, and bathe his body in water, and shall be unclean until evening.

pob.text: And everyone who touches any object on which she sits shall wash his clothes and bathe in water[a], and he shall be unclean until the evening.

spob.text: Anyone who touches any object she sits on must wash their clothes and bathe in water. They will be ritually unclean until evening.

public_domain_references.bsb: Whoever touches any furniture on which she was sitting must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he will be unclean until evening.
public_domain_references.web: Whoever touches anything that she sits on shall wash his clothes, and bathe himself in water, and be unclean until the evening.
public_domain_references.asv: And whosoever toucheth anything that she sitteth upon shall wash his clothes, and bathe himself in water, and be unclean until the even.
public_domain_references.kjv: And whosoever toucheth any thing that she sat upon shall wash his clothes, and bathe [himself] in water, and be unclean until the even.
public_domain_references.brenton: And every one that touches any vessel on which she shall sit, shall wash his garments and bathe himself in water, and shall be unclean until evening.

pob.text: And if it is on the bed or on the item on which she sits[a], when he touches it he shall be unclean until the evening.

spob.text: And if the thing he touches is on the bed or on an item she sits on, he will be ritually unclean until evening.

public_domain_references.bsb: And whether it is a bed or furniture on which she was sitting, whoever touches it will be unclean until evening.
public_domain_references.web: If it is on the bed, or on anything she sits on, when he touches it, he shall be unclean until the evening.
public_domain_references.asv: And if it be on the bed, or on anything whereon she sitteth, when he toucheth it, he shall be unclean until the even.
public_domain_references.kjv: And if it [be] on [her] bed, or on any thing whereon she sitteth, when he toucheth it, he shall be unclean until the even.
public_domain_references.brenton: And whether it be while she is on her bed, or on a seat which she may happen to sit upon when he touches her, he shall be unclean till evening.

pob.text: If a man indeed lies with her[a], and her menstrual impurity comes upon him, he shall be unclean seven days, and every bed on which he lies shall be unclean.

spob.text: If a man does have sexual intercourse with her and her menstrual impurity comes upon him, he will be ritually unclean for seven days. Every bed he lies on will also be ritually unclean.

public_domain_references.bsb: If a man lies with her and her menstrual flow touches him, he will be unclean for seven days, and any bed on which he lies will become unclean.
public_domain_references.web: “‘If any man lies with her, and her monthly flow is on him, he shall be unclean seven days; and every bed he lies on shall be unclean.
public_domain_references.asv: And if any man lie with her, and her impurity be upon him, he shall be unclean seven days; and every bed whereon he lieth shall be unclean.
public_domain_references.kjv: And if any man lie with her at all, and her flowers be upon him, he shall be unclean seven days; and all the bed whereon he lieth shall be unclean.
public_domain_references.brenton: And if any one shall lie with her, and her uncleanness be upon him, he shall be unclean seven days; and every bed on which he shall have lain shall be unclean.

pob.text: If a woman has a discharge of blood for many days[a], not at the time of her menstrual impurity, or if she has a discharge beyond her menstrual impurity, all the days of her unclean discharge she shall be unclean[b], as in the days of her menstrual impurity.

spob.text: If a woman has a flow of blood for many days outside her time of menstrual impurity, or if the bleeding continues beyond that time, she will be ritually unclean for as long as the bleeding lasts, just as she is during her menstrual impurity.

public_domain_references.bsb: When a woman has a discharge of her blood for many days at a time other than her menstrual period, or if it continues beyond her period, she will be unclean all the days of her unclean discharge, just as she is during the days of her menstruation.
public_domain_references.web: “‘If a woman has a discharge of her blood many days not in the time of her period, or if she has a discharge beyond the time of her period, all the days of the discharge of her uncleanness shall be as in the days of her period. She is unclean.
public_domain_references.asv: And if a woman have an issue of her blood many days not in the time of her impurity, or if she have an issue beyond the time of her impurity; all the days of the issue of her uncleanness she shall be as in the days of her impurity: she is unclean.
public_domain_references.kjv: And if a woman have an issue of her blood many days out of the time of her separation, or if it run beyond the time of her separation; all the days of the issue of her uncleanness shall be as the days of her separation: she [shall be] unclean.
public_domain_references.brenton: And if a woman have an issue of blood many days, not in the time of her separation; if the blood should also flow after her separation, all the days of the issue of her uncleanness [shall be] as the days of her separation: she shall be unclean.

pob.text: Every bed on which she lies during all the days of her discharge shall be to her like the bed of her menstruation[a], and every vessel on which she sits shall be unclean[b], like the uncleanness of her menstruation.

spob.text: Every bed she lies on while the discharge continues will be ritually unclean, just like a bed she lies on during menstruation. Every object she sits on will also be ritually unclean, just like an object she sits on during menstruation.

public_domain_references.bsb: Any bed on which she lies or any furniture on which she sits during the days of her discharge will be unclean, like her bed during her menstrual period.
public_domain_references.web: Every bed she lies on all the days of her discharge shall be to her as the bed of her period. Everything she sits on shall be unclean, as the uncleanness of her period.
public_domain_references.asv: Every bed whereon she lieth all the days of her issue shall be unto her as the bed of her impurity: and everything whereon she sitteth shall be unclean, as the uncleanness of her impurity.

spob.text: But if a house in a walled city is not redeemed—that is, bought back—within one full year, it will permanently belong to the buyer and the buyer’s family for all future generations. Even at the Jubilee, it will not return to the original owner’s family.[a]

public_domain_references.web: If it isn’t redeemed within the space of a full year, then the house that is in the walled city shall be made sure in perpetuity to him who bought it, throughout his generations. It shall not be released in the Jubilee.
public_domain_references.asv: And if it be not redeemed within the space of a full year, then the house that is in the walled city shall be made sure in perpetuity to him that bought it, throughout his generations: it shall not go out in the jubilee.
public_domain_references.kjv: And if it be not redeemed within the space of a full year, then the house that [is] in the walled city shall be established for ever to him that bought it throughout his generations: it shall not go out in the jubile.
public_domain_references.brenton: And if it be not ransomed until there be completed of its time a full year, the house which is in the walled city shall be surely confirmed to him that bought it, throughout his generations; and it shall not go out in the release.

pob.text: But the houses of the villages that have no wall around them shall be regarded as the fields of the land[a]; redemption shall be available for them[b], and in the Jubilee they shall go out.

spob.text: But houses in villages without surrounding walls must be treated like rural land. The right to buy them back remains, and in the Jubilee year they must be released from the sale.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: But houses in villages with no walls around them are to be considered as open fields. They may be redeemed, and they shall be released in the Jubilee.
public_domain_references.web: But the houses of the villages which have no wall around them shall be accounted for with the fields of the country: they may be redeemed, and they shall be released in the Jubilee.
public_domain_references.asv: But the houses of the villages which have no wall round about them shall be reckoned with the fields of the country: they may be redeemed, and they shall go out in the jubilee.
public_domain_references.kjv: But the houses of the villages which have no wall round about them shall be counted as the fields of the country: they may be redeemed, and they shall go out in the jubile.
public_domain_references.brenton: But the houses in the villages which have not a wall round about them, shall be reckoned as the fields of the country: they shall always be redeemable, and they shall go out in the release.

pob.text: As for the cities of the Levites[a], the houses in the cities of their possession may be redeemed permanently by the Levites.

spob.text: In the cities belonging to the Levites, they always have the right[a] to buy back houses there.

public_domain_references.bsb: As for the cities of the Levites, the Levites always have the right to redeem their houses in the cities they possess.
public_domain_references.web: “‘Nevertheless, in the cities of the Levites, the Levites may redeem the houses in the cities of their possession at any time.
public_domain_references.asv: Nevertheless the cities of the Levites, the houses of the cities of their possession, may the Levites redeem at any time.
public_domain_references.kjv: Notwithstanding the cities of the Levites, [and] the houses of the cities of their possession, may the Levites redeem at any time.
public_domain_references.brenton: And the cities of the Levites, the houses of the cities in their possession, shall be always redeemable to the Levites.

pob.text: And if one of the Levites redeems it[a], then the sale of the house in the city of his possession shall be released in the Jubilee[b]; for the houses of the cities of the Levites are their possession among the sons of Israel.

spob.text: If one of the Levites redeems a house in a city belonging to him, the house must be released from the sale in the Jubilee year. This is because the houses in the Levites’ cities are their property among the sons of Israel.

public_domain_references.bsb: So whatever belongs to the Levites may be redeemed—a house sold in a city they possess—and must be released in the Jubilee, because the houses in the cities of the Levites are their possession among the Israelites.
public_domain_references.web: The Levites may redeem the house that was sold, and the city of his possession, and it shall be released in the Jubilee; for the houses of the cities of the Levites are their possession among the children of Israel.
public_domain_references.asv: And if one of the Levites redeem, then the house that was sold, and the city of his possession, shall go out in the jubilee; for the houses of the cities of the Levites are their possession among the children of Israel.
public_domain_references.kjv: And if a man purchase of the Levites, then the house that was sold, and the city of his possession, shall go out in [the year of] jubile: for the houses of the cities of the Levites [are] their possession among the children of Israel.
public_domain_references.brenton: And if any one shall redeem a house of the Levites, then shall their sale of the houses of their possession go out in the release; because the houses of the cities of the Levites are their possession in the midst of the children of Israel.

pob.text: But the field of pastureland belonging to their cities must not be sold[b][a], for it is their permanent possession.

spob.text: But the pastureland belonging to their cities must not be sold, because it is their permanent possession.

public_domain_references.bsb: But the open pastureland around their cities may not be sold, for this is their permanent possession.
public_domain_references.web: But the field of the pasture lands of their cities may not be sold, for it is their perpetual possession.
public_domain_references.asv: But the field of the suburbs of their cities may not be sold; for it is their perpetual possession.
public_domain_references.kjv: But the field of the suburbs of their cities may not be sold; for it [is] their perpetual possession.
public_domain_references.brenton: And the lands set apart for their cities shall not be sold, because this is their perpetual possession.

pob.text: If your brother becomes poor and his hand falters beside you[a], then you shall support him[b]; so that he may live beside you as a resident foreigner or a temporary resident.

spob.text: If your brother becomes poor and can no longer support himself while living among you,[a] you must help him so that he can keep living beside you as a resident foreigner or a temporary resident.[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: Now if your countryman becomes destitute and cannot support himself among you, then you are to help him as you would a foreigner or stranger, so that he can continue to live among you.
public_domain_references.web: “‘If your brother has become poor, and his hand can’t support himself among you, then you shall uphold him. He shall live with you like an alien and a temporary resident.
public_domain_references.asv: And if thy brother be waxed poor, and his hand fail with thee; then thou shalt uphold him: [as] a stranger and a sojourner shall he live with thee.
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ And if thy brother be waxen poor, and fallen in decay with thee; then thou shalt relieve him: [yea, though he be] a stranger, or a sojourner; that he may live with thee.
public_domain_references.brenton: And if thy brother who is with thee become poor, and he fail in resources with thee, thou shalt help him as a stranger and a sojourner, and thy brother shall live with thee.

pob.text: Do not take interest or profit from him[a], but fear your God[b], and let your brother live with you.

spob.text: Do not charge him interest or make a profit from lending to him. Instead, fear your God, and let your brother live with you.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Do not take any interest or profit from him, but fear your God, that your countryman may live among you.
public_domain_references.web: Take no interest from him or profit; but fear your God, that your brother may live among you.
public_domain_references.asv: Take thou no interest of him or increase, but fear thy God; that thy brother may live with thee.
public_domain_references.kjv: Take thou no usury of him, or increase: but fear thy God; that thy brother may live with thee.
public_domain_references.brenton: Thou shalt not receive from him interest, nor increase: and thou shalt fear thy God: I [am] the Lord: and thy brother shall live with thee.

pob.text: You shall not lend him your money at interest[b][a], nor give him your food for increase.

spob.text: Do not charge him interest when you lend him your money. Do not make a profit when you supply him with your food.

public_domain_references.bsb: You must not lend him your silver at interest or sell him your food for profit.
public_domain_references.web: You shall not lend him your money at interest, nor give him your food for profit.
public_domain_references.asv: Thou shalt not give him thy money upon interest, nor give him thy victuals for increase.
public_domain_references.kjv: Thou shalt not give him thy money upon usury, nor lend him thy victuals for increase.
public_domain_references.brenton: Thou shalt not lend thy money to him at interest, and thou shalt not lend thy meat to him to be returned with increase.

pob.text: I am Yahweh your God[a], who brought you out of the land of Egypt to give you the land of Canaan, to be your God.

spob.text: I am Yahweh[a], your God. I brought you out of the land of Egypt to give you the land of Canaan and to be your God.

public_domain_references.bsb: I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt to give you the land of Canaan and to be your God.
public_domain_references.web: I am Yahweh your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, to give you the land of Canaan, and to be your God.
public_domain_references.asv: I am Jehovah your God, who brought you forth out of the land of Egypt, to give you the land of Canaan, [and] to be your God.
public_domain_references.kjv: I [am] the LORD your God, which brought you forth out of the land of Egypt, to give you the land of Canaan, [and] to be your God.
public_domain_references.brenton: I [am] the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, to give you the land of Chanaan, so as to be your God.

pob.text: And if your brother becomes poor with you and sells himself to you[b][a], you shall not make him serve as a slave.

spob.text: If your brother becomes poor among you and sells himself to you,[a] do not make him work as a slave.

public_domain_references.bsb: If a countryman among you becomes destitute and sells himself to you, then you must not force him into slave labor.
public_domain_references.web: “‘If your brother has grown poor among you, and sells himself to you, you shall not make him to serve as a slave.
public_domain_references.asv: And if thy brother be waxed poor with thee, and sell himself unto thee; thou shalt not make him to serve as a bondservant.
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ And if thy brother [that dwelleth] by thee be waxen poor, and be sold unto thee; thou shalt not compel him to serve as a bondservant:
public_domain_references.brenton: And if thy brother by thee be lowered, and be sold to thee, he shall not serve thee with the servitude of a slave.

pob.text: He shall be with you like a hired worker[a], like a sojourner; he shall serve with you until the year of jubilee.

spob.text: He must remain with you as a hired worker, like a resident foreigner. He must work with you until the year of jubilee.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Let him stay with you as a hired worker or temporary resident; he is to work for you until the Year of Jubilee.
public_domain_references.web: As a hired servant, and as a temporary resident, he shall be with you; he shall serve with you until the Year of Jubilee.
public_domain_references.asv: As a hired servant, and as a sojourner, he shall be with thee; he shall serve with thee unto the year of jubilee:
public_domain_references.kjv: [But] as an hired servant, [and] as a sojourner, he shall be with thee, [and] shall serve thee unto the year of jubile:
public_domain_references.brenton: He shall be with thee as a hireling or a sojourner, he shall work for thee till the year of release:

pob.text: Then he and his sons with him shall go out from you[b][a], and he shall return to his clan and return to the property of his fathers.

spob.text: Then he and his sons will leave you together. He will return to his clan[a] and to his ancestral property.

public_domain_references.bsb: Then he and his children are to be released, and he may return to his clan and to the property of his fathers.
public_domain_references.web: Then he shall go out from you, he and his children with him, and shall return to his own family, and to the possession of his fathers.
public_domain_references.asv: then shall he go out from thee, he and his children with him, and shall return unto his own family, and unto the possession of his fathers shall he return.
public_domain_references.kjv: And [then] shall he depart from thee, [both] he and his children with him, and shall return unto his own family, and unto the possession of his fathers shall he return.
public_domain_references.brenton: and he shall go out in the release, and his children with him; and he shall go to his family, he shall hasten back to his patrimony.

pob.text: For they are my slaves[a], whom I brought out from the land of Egypt[b]; they shall not be sold as slaves are sold.

spob.text: For they are my slaves[a]. I brought them out of Egypt, so they must not be sold as ordinary slave property.

public_domain_references.bsb: Because the Israelites are My servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt, they are not to be sold as slaves.
public_domain_references.web: For they are my servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt. They shall not be sold as slaves.
public_domain_references.asv: For they are my servants, whom I brought forth out of the land of Egypt: they shall not be sold as bondmen.
public_domain_references.kjv: For they [are] my servants, which I brought forth out of the land of Egypt: they shall not be sold as bondmen.
public_domain_references.brenton: Because these are my servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt; such an one shall not be sold as a [common] servant.

pob.text: You shall not rule over him harshly[a], but you shall fear your God.

spob.text: Do not use your power over him to treat him harshly. Instead, fear your God.

public_domain_references.bsb: You are not to rule over them harshly, but you shall fear your God.
public_domain_references.web: You shall not rule over him with harshness, but shall fear your God.
public_domain_references.asv: Thou shalt not rule over him with rigor, but shalt fear thy God.
public_domain_references.kjv: Thou shalt not rule over him with rigour; but shalt fear thy God.
public_domain_references.brenton: Thou shalt not oppress him with labour, and shalt fear the Lord thy God.

pob.text: As for your male slave and your female slave who may belong to you[a], from the nations that are around you[b], from them you may buy a male slave and a female slave.

spob.text: You may buy male and female slaves from the non-Israelite peoples around you, and they may belong to you.

public_domain_references.bsb: Your menservants and maidservants shall come from the nations around you, from whom you may purchase them.
public_domain_references.web: “‘As for your male and your female slaves, whom you may have from the nations that are around you, from them you may buy male and female slaves.
public_domain_references.asv: And as for thy bondmen, and thy bondmaids, whom thou shalt have; of the nations that are round about you, of them shall ye buy bondmen and bondmaids.
public_domain_references.kjv: Both thy bondmen, and thy bondmaids, which thou shalt have, [shall be] of the heathen that are round about you; of them shall ye buy bondmen and bondmaids.
public_domain_references.brenton: And whatever number of men-servants and maid-servants thou shalt have, thou shalt purchase male and female servants from the nations that are round about thee.

pob.text: You may also buy from the sons of the sojourners who reside with you[a], and from their families who are with you, whom they have fathered in your land[b]; and they shall become your possession.

spob.text: You may also buy descendants of the resident foreigners who live among you. You may buy members of their families who were born to them in your land. They will become your property.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: You may also purchase them from the foreigners residing among you or their clans living among you who are born in your land. These may become your property.
public_domain_references.web: Moreover, of the children of the aliens who live among you, of them you may buy, and of their families who are with you, which they have conceived in your land; and they will be your property.
public_domain_references.asv: Moreover of the children of the strangers that sojourn among you, of them shall ye buy, and of their families that are with you, which they have begotten in your land: and they shall be your possession.
public_domain_references.kjv: Moreover of the children of the strangers that do sojourn among you, of them shall ye buy, and of their families that [are] with you, which they begat in your land: and they shall be your possession.
public_domain_references.brenton: And of the sons of the sojourners that are among you, of these ye shall buy and of their relations, all that shall be in your lands; let them be to you for a possession.

pob.text: You may pass them on as an inheritance to your sons after you[a], to inherit as a possession permanently; from them you may exact labor. But over your brothers, the sons of Israel[b], no man shall rule over his brother harshly.

spob.text: You may leave them as an inheritance to your sons after you. They may be your sons’ permanent property, and you may make them work. But no man may rule harshly over his brother, a son of Israel.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: You may leave them to your sons after you to inherit as property; you can make them slaves for life. But as for your brothers, the Israelites, no man may rule harshly over his brother.
public_domain_references.web: You may make them an inheritance for your children after you, to hold for a possession. Of them you may take your slaves forever, but over your brothers the children of Israel you shall not rule, one over another, with harshness.
public_domain_references.asv: And ye shall make them an inheritance for your children after you, to hold for a possession; of them shall ye take your bondmen for ever: but over your brethren the children of Israel ye shall not rule, one over another, with rigor.
public_domain_references.kjv: And ye shall take them as an inheritance for your children after you, to inherit [them for] a possession; they shall be your bondmen for ever: but over your brethren the children of Israel, ye shall not rule one over another with rigour.
public_domain_references.brenton: And ye shall distribute them to your children after you, and they shall be to you permanent possessions for ever: but of your brethren the children of Israel, one shall not oppress his brother in labours.

pob.text: If the means of a resident foreigner among you become sufficient[a], and your brother beside him becomes poor and sells himself to the resident foreigner among you, or to a member of the foreigner’s clan,

public_domain_references.brenton: And if a stranger or sojourner with thee wax rich, and thy brother in distress be sold to the stranger or the sojourner that is with thee, or to a proselyte by extraction;

pob.text: He shall calculate with his buyer from the year he sold himself to him until the year of jubilee[a], and the price of his sale shall be according to the number of years[b]; like the days of a hired worker he shall be with him.

public_domain_references.kjv: If [there be] yet many years [behind], according unto them he shall give again the price of his redemption out of the money that he was bought for.
public_domain_references.brenton: And if any have a greater number of years [than enough], according to these he shall pay his ransom out of his purchase-money.

pob.text: For the sons of Israel are my servants[a]; they are my servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt[b]. I am Yahweh your God.

spob.text: For the sons of Israel belong to me as slaves.[a] They are my slaves, whom I brought out of Egypt. I am Yahweh your God.

pob.text: And I will destroy your high places[a], and cut down your incense altars, and place your corpses on the carcasses of your idols[b], and my soul will abhor you.

spob.text: I will destroy your shrines on the heights and cut down your incense altars.[a] I will lay your corpses on the corpses of your idols,[b] and my soul will loathe you.

pob.text: And I will make your cities a ruin[a], and I will lay waste your sanctuaries, and I will not smell the pleasing aroma of your offerings.

public_domain_references.brenton: And I will lay your cities waste, and I will make your sanctuaries desolate, and I will not smell the savour of your sacrifices.

pob.text: And I myself will lay the land waste[a], and your enemies who dwell in it will be appalled at it.

spob.text: I myself will devastate the land, and your enemies who live there will be appalled[a] by its devastation.

public_domain_references.brenton: And I will lay your land desolate, and your enemies who dwell in it shall wonder at it.

pob.text: And I will scatter you among the nations[a], and I will draw out the sword after you; and your land will become a desolation, and your cities will become ruins.

spob.text: I will scatter you among the nations and draw the sword to pursue you. Your land will become desolate, and your cities will become ruins.

pob.text: Then the land will enjoy its Sabbaths all the days of its desolation[a], while you are in the land of your enemies; then the land will rest and enjoy its Sabbaths.

spob.text: Throughout the time the land lies desolate, it will rest. It will have the Sabbath rest[a] it did not have while you were living on it.

public_domain_references.brenton: And ye shall be in the land of your enemies; then the land shall keep its sabbaths, and the land shall enjoy its sabbaths all the days of its desolation: it shall keep sabbaths which it kept not among your sabbaths, when ye dwelt in it.

pob.text: As for those of you who remain, I will bring faintness into their hearts in the lands of their enemies, and the sound of a driven leaf will pursue them; they will flee as one flees from the sword, and they will fall when no one is pursuing.

spob.text: As for those of you who remain, I will make their hearts lose courage in the lands of their enemies. The sound of a leaf blown along will chase them. They will flee as people flee from a sword, and they will fall even though no one is chasing them.

public_domain_references.kjv: And upon them that are left [alive] of you I will send a faintness into their hearts in the lands of their enemies; and the sound of a shaken leaf shall chase them; and they shall flee, as fleeing from a sword; and they shall fall when none pursueth.
public_domain_references.brenton: And to those who are left of you I will bring bondage into their heart in the land of their enemies; and the sound of a shaken leaf shall chase them, and they shall flee as fleeing from war, and shall fall when none pursues them.

pob.text: They will stumble over one another as if before a sword[a], though no one is pursuing[b]; and you will have no power to stand before your enemies.

public_domain_references.kjv: And they shall fall one upon another, as it were before a sword, when none pursueth: and ye shall have no power to stand before your enemies.
public_domain_references.brenton: And brother shall disregard brother as in war, when none pursues; and ye shall not be able to withstand your enemies.

pob.text: And those of you who remain will waste away in the lands of your enemies because of their iniquity[b][a]; and also because of the iniquities of their fathers with them they will waste away.

pob.text: Then I will remember my covenant with Jacob[a], and also my covenant with Isaac, and also my covenant with Abraham I will remember; and I will remember the land.

pob.text: But the land will be abandoned by them and will enjoy its Sabbaths while it lies desolate without them[a], and they will accept the punishment for their iniquity, because—indeed, because—they rejected my judgments and their soul abhorred my statutes.

pob.text: Yet even then[a], when they are in the land of their enemies, I will not reject them, and I will not abhor them so as to destroy them, to break my covenant with them[c][b]; for I am Yahweh their God.

spob.text: Yet even then, while they are living in the land of their enemies, I will not reject them or loathe them to the point of destroying them and breaking my covenant with them. For I am Yahweh[a] their God.

pob.text: But I will remember for them the covenant with their forefathers, whom I brought out from the land of Egypt in the sight of the nations, to be their God: I am Yahweh.

public_domain_references.kjv: He shall not search whether it be good or bad, neither shall he change it: and if he change it at all, then both it and the change thereof shall be holy; it shall not be redeemed.
public_domain_references.brenton: Thou shalt not change a good for a bad, or a bad for a good; and if thou shouldest at all change it, its equivalent also shall be holy, it shall not be redeemed.
